title: When plans change
intro: Prices change and weeks get skipped. A good plan bends instead of breaking.
explanation: Plans change all the time, and that's normal. A price can go up or down. Your weekly saving can change. A gift can arrive, or a week's allowance can be skipped.
When something changes, work out the new numbers first: what's left to save, and how many weeks that takes now.
Then pick a calm fix. You could wait a bit longer, save a little more each week, or choose a different goal. Any of these is fine.

example.title: When a price goes up
lines: Ari saves {m:500} a week for a {m:4000} goal. That's 8 weeks.
The price goes up to {m:4500}. Now it's 9 weeks.
Fix 2: save {m:600} a week instead. Then it's still 8 weeks.

practice.prompt: You're just starting to save {m:400} a week for a {m:2000} goal. The price drops to {m:1600}. How many weeks now?

misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. That's the old price. Work it out with {m:1600}.

practice.wrong: Not quite. Use the new price, then count the weeks.
hints: Count up to {m:1600} in steps of {m:400}.
practice.correct: That's it. 4 weeks, one week sooner than before.
